Reference / http/websocket

http/websocket#

WebSocket connections (RFC 6455): messages, limits and close codes.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

for await connection -> message {
    await connection.send_text(message.text().upper());
}
await connection.send_json(Json(JsonField("ok", true)));
await connection.close(code: 1000, reason: "bye");

Description#

WebSocket connections (RFC 6455): messages, limits and close codes.

A message is text or binary; asking a binary one for text is WebSocketMessageIsNotText. message() throws WebSocketClosed once the connection has closed, next() answers none, so a for await loop ends. Messages are bounded by WebSocketLimits (16 MiB per message, 64 KiB per frame, 16 queued by default). A server opens connections through http/websocket_server, a client through http/websocket_client.

object WebSocketClose#

object WebSocketClose

Wire close values. 1005/1006/1015 remain reporting outcomes, never emissions. Registered application codes 3000/3003/3008 are pinned from IANA 2026-10-12; private application codes 4000..4999 require no registration.

code (1000-1003, 1007-1014, 3000, 3003, 3008 or 4000-4999) with a reason of at most 123 bytes; WebSocketFailure otherwise.

role WebSocketConnection#

role WebSocketConnection

A WebSocket connection, walked message by message (#220):

for await connection -> message {
    await connection.send_text(message.text().upper());
}

message() waits for the next message and throws WebSocketClosed once the connection has closed; next() answers none instead, so the loop ends.
